title: Telehealth Compliance Anchored To Participant Proposal
content: A participant operating AI-assisted prescription renewal must adhere to Utah's telehealth provider requirements in §26B-4-704, with specific subsections deemed satisfied by following protocols described in the participant's Proposal (Schedule B): Doctronic Parts 2B and 3B; Legion Proposal section 4. Certain subsections (e.g., the patient-records portability default) are inapplicable; others are substituted by Proposal-section conformance.
pub:source_review_unresolved: No retained source gives a Commencement Date or publishes the Section 2.B commencement notice; the register said the demonstration period had not started when retrieved 2026-09-24.
The register lists malpractice insurance covering AI-related liability, but no insurance term appears in the retained signed agreement text.
The UAC R156-1 link returned HTTP 404 and was removed; no current official Office of Administrative Rules URL was retained.
The PubLedge JIA and its 30-minute re-display term remain an unpublished draft and are not statutory terms.
Utah HB 452 section 13-72a-203 uses a seven-day interaction condition rather than the draft JIA 30-minute resumption condition.
The EveryAILaw target identities and cross-owner existence remain federation assertions; this receipt does not make EveryAILaw an issuing authority or certify current law.
The sb149-learning-lab-and-ai-defense and hb452-mental-health-chatbot-stack mappings are kept and qualified, not removed; whether to remap them is a human decision.
The disclose-genai-on-first-session obligation id and name still say 'first session'; its text was corrected in a separate receipt.
This is selected-clause source consistency, not a complete current-law/applicability or agency-interpretation certification. No human verification date renewed.
SB226 current-codification locator/identity gap remains outside this HB452-only tranche; no new acceptance of its unchanged general-disclosure clauses.
